To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) imaging surrogates and biomarkers are of increasing importance to evaluate novel therapeutic agents; (2) validation and proof-of-mechanism are the most important criteria for the use of imaging surrogate parameters; (3) novel imaging approaches provide structural, physiological, and metabolic information and annotate structure with molecular information; and (4) the design of target-specific imaging probes should start early in the drug development process.
imaging biomarkers are important in preclinical drug evaluation and in clinical drug evaluation.
Imaging biomarkers can be used for the evaluation of novel therapeutics in preclinical studies and in clinical trials, provided they are properly validated and the data are appropriately analyzed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development, validation and clinical application of imaging biomarkers.
the development and application of imaging biomarkers to assess the efficacy of novel therapeutic interventions.
the development of imaging biomarkers and the validation and implementation of imaging surrogates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
imaging biomarkers and imaging surrogates are a valuable addition to the clinical drug development toolbox.
imaging biomarkers are a valuable and indispensable component of the preclinical and early clinical drug development.
imaging biomarkers are an integral part of the drug discovery process and will be increasingly important for drug evaluation in clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the combination of PET and MR imaging is a very powerful tool for preclinical and clinical research.
the use of imaging readouts as surrogate markers for the evaluation of therapeutic agents has to be further developed and validated.
imaging biomarkers can provide valuable information in the early phases of drug development, and can be used to support decisions on the further development of a drug candidate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of imaging readouts as biomarker or surrogate parameters for therapeutic evaluation is a promising and rapidly developing field.
the imaging biomarker concept is a powerful tool to improve the drug evaluation process and to accelerate drug development.
imaging biomarkers are a promising tool for the evaluation of novel therapies, and their use in the clinical setting should be further encouraged.
